body:
BuildTestEmbedded's teardown-confirmation work observed a directory's committed child disappear when a clock callback re-entered FakeFileSystem. Round-2 review then demonstrated three neighboring paths in the -2 artifact that could replace a populated directory: must-create open, symlink creation and move. This change is part of the BuildTest utilization / projections campaign tracked in handoff url://handoff/handoffs/hf-2026-08-24-fix-startup-compaction-delta-heap-exhaustion-then-revalidate-the-extreme-suite.

Round-3 review reproduced two remaining lookup defects in -3: a move through a final dangling destination link replaced an unrelated populated directory, and clock-driven link replacement let reads report a child that never existed at the requested path. Inherited `createDirectories` could therefore return success without creating that path. The correction belongs to the fork's lookup layer.

Every primitive mutator resolves symlinks, validates its target and applies its change inside ONE critical section. The clock finishes before the lock; recursive resolution reuses the captured time. Canonicalization, metadata and listing also resolve and construct their result under the lock after callbacks. A dangling link is an error where an existing target is required and never redirects a mutation to a sibling. `atomicMove` checks and replaces the final destination entry itself, including a dangling or live link, with a matching parent and segment; its referent and unrelated siblings survive. Inherited `createDirectories` receives current directory metadata and creates the requested components in the callback scenario. Its separate primitive calls do not gain a whole-composition guarantee against independently concurrent edits.

Review credits: [revokio1's entry-admission review](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/revokio1-evidence/evidence/revokio1) supplied the prior callback proofs; [revokio2's symlink review](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/revokio2-evidence/evidence/revokio2) identified both remaining defects and supplied the five adopted public reproducers. [revokio3's independent review](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/revokio3-evidence/evidence/revokio3) verified the primitive lock boundaries, unchanged public API and 94/94 first-attempt tests, and identified the compound-method scope limitation now stated in README.

Published coordinate: `com.squareup.okio:okio-fakefilesystem-jvm:3.4.0-r576-registry-lock-4` at [kotlin.directory](https://kotlin.directory/com/squareup/okio/okio-fakefilesystem-jvm/3.4.0-r576-registry-lock-4/). Public JVM declarations, class names and dependency versions are unchanged from -3.

Validation:

- README scope correction: the module script ran once after the documentation edit, with 94/94 passing first-attempt native XML rows and zero failures/errors/skips/attempt-history. [Documentation follow-up evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/okiofix4-evidence/evidence/okiofix4) retains the XML audit. No source or existing-test edits were made in this follow-up.
- Five unchanged reviewer reproducers: move proof 3/3 assertion-red on -3; metadata, canonicalization, listing and inherited directory creation each 3/3 assertion-red (12/12).
- Three additional public boundaries each assertion-red 3/3: existing dangling destination, existing live destination with differing referent basename, and final dangling-link canonicalization. Total new red-first rows: 24/24; all prior 70/70 pass.
- Product-only control restores only the old product source, retaining new tests and -4 scripts. Its rebuilt JAR equals served -3 byte-for-byte; all 24/24 new rows are assertion-red again and all 70/70 prior rows pass.
- [Exact-source GitHub-machine gate](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/actions/runs/39020635632) checks out [d5151e217294a9b0aa4b6a2210fdf09c977c383d](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/commit/d5151e217294a9b0aa4b6a2210fdf09c977c383d): 94/94 passing FIRST-attempt native rows: required move 3/3, four read proofs 4×3/3, three extra boundaries 3×3/3, and prior 70/70; zero failures/errors/skips/attempt-history. All 20 registry trials pass. No additional test batch followed this accepted gate.
- The actual build compares every compiled class name and public `javap` declaration with checksum-verified -3; declarations are identical, satisfying the named-public-API superset check. POM changes only the project version and adds no runtime dependency.
- Tested/published JAR SHA-256: `a711455100fde7bc16432e583216d10b58f66bba72e1c424363a8718d622eace`; POM SHA-256: `28f6648942e359711ab1530b68e8cebe71bb3f5e4516fb52fe4794173a6430e0`. Served bytes verified against the exact accepted gate bytes.
- [Round-3 evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/okiofakefs3-evidence/evidence/okiofakefs3) contains native XML, control output and publication provenance. [Round-2 evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/okiofakefs2-evidence/evidence/okiofakefs2) retains 39/39 prior entry-admission red proofs and the 70/70 accepted -3 gate. [Round-1 evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/okio/tree/wip/okiofakefs1-evidence/evidence/okiofakefs1) retains the directory proofs.

Existing-test edits: none. All prior test sources, assertions, timeouts and iteration counts remain unchanged. New reviewer source files are byte-identical to the evidence; only the counted move method is selected from the file containing the review's separately refuted exploratory methods. The standalone runner adds these five scenarios and three additional public boundary scenarios. No investigation output or temporary workflow is in this branch. Known inherited core `createDirectories(existingFile)` behavior remains unchanged, as established in the review.

The [consumer documentation branch](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/BuildTestEmbedded/tree/wip/okiofakefs1-docs) records the prior defect classes and -3; the orchestrator can incorporate this round's evidence and version. Consumer dependency selection, full-suite CI monitoring and merging belong to the orchestrator. No merge, deployment or production-host action was performed.
